sources.quote: Cannon conjectured in the early 1990s that the converse holds

Every word-hyperbolic group G whose Gromov boundary is homeomorphic to S^2 admits a homomorphism to Isom(H^3) with finite kernel whose action on H^3 is proper and cocompact. If G is torsion-free it is the fundamental group of a closed hyperbolic 3-manifold.
Bonk-Kleiner (Inventiones 2002/ Geom. Topol. 2005) proved it when the Ahlfors-regular conformal dimension is attained
31-page analytic proof: reduces via Bourdon-Kleiner's modulus criterion to a uniform bound on combinatorial 2-modulus

plain: If a group looks like a sphere from far away, it really is a symmetry group of hyperbolic 3-space

steps: The group's boundary at infinity is a topological sphere
New: curve families can't get too thick at any scale
So the sphere can be made round, and the group acts on $\mathbb{H}^3$
